For birdwatchers looking to branch out and meet people outside the birding community, there are several wonderful outdoor hobbies to consider. 

Sailing is an excellent way to spend time on the water and meet people through local yacht clubs or crew finder boards, as boats often need multiple people to operate. The estimated start-up cost is around $1,500 for beginner lessons, basic sailing gear, and introductory club fees, making it one of the most expensive options to get into.

Taking up landscape and architecture photography offers a great reason to be outside while connecting with local photography groups and photowalk clubs. Getting started requires an estimated cost of $800 for a solid entry-level mirrorless camera and a versatile lens. 

Cycling is a fantastic way to enjoy the outdoors in a highly social setting, as most towns have local cycling clubs that organize weekly group rides for various skill levels. You can expect an estimated start-up cost of $600 for a reliable entry-level hybrid or road bike, some basic maintenance gear, and a good helmet.

Joining a community garden provides a peaceful outdoor environment where you can easily strike up conversations with neighboring plot owners who share an interest in growing food and flowers. The estimated start-up cost is roughly $100, which covers a seasonal plot rental fee, basic hand tools, soil amendments, and seeds.

Pickleball has taken over public outdoor courts everywhere and is famously welcoming to beginners, offering an incredibly easy way to socialize with people from all walks of life in a fun, active setting. The estimated start-up cost is only about $50 to purchase a quality beginner paddle and a few outdoor balls.
